Standardized differences of a linear fixed-effect fit

Source: R/standardize_linear_fe.R
standardize.linear_fe.Rd

Indirect or direct standardization of every provider's mean outcome, as a difference from the expected mean.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'linear_fe'
standardize(
  fit,
  type = c("indirect", "direct"),
  null = "median",
  providers = NULL,
  gamma_se = NULL,
  level = NULL,
  ci = c("wald", "robust_wald"),
  wald_variance = c("case_mix", "full"),
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

a model fitted by fit_linear_fe().

type

"indirect" (default) or "direct".

null

for indirect standardization, the norm of the provider effect: "median" (default), "mean" (weighted by rows) or a number.

providers

optional subset of provider identifiers.

gamma_se

optional standard errors of the provider effects, named by provider (for instance the se column of a test() result); with them se_difference is returned.

level

if given, confidence limits of the difference are added, mapped from Wald limits of \(\gamma_i\).

ci

the standard error of the limits: "wald" (default; model-based, with wald_variance) or "robust_wald", see confint.linear_fe().

wald_variance

"case_mix" (default) or "full", see gamma_variance().

alternative

"two.sided" (default), "greater" or "less".

...

unused.

Value

A data frame with one row per provider: provider, observed, expected, difference, and when requested se_difference, lower, upper. Attributes type, null_value, level.

Details

With \(\mu_{ij}(\gamma) = \gamma + Z_{ij}^\top\hat\beta\):

  • indirect: observed \(O_i = \sum_{j \in i} Y_{ij}\), expected \(E_i = \sum_{j \in i} \mu_{ij}(\gamma_0)\), difference \((O_i - E_i) / n_i = \hat\gamma_i - \gamma_0\);

  • direct: expected \(E_i = \sum_k \mu_k(\hat\gamma_i)\) over every fitted row, observed \(O = \sum_k Y_k\), difference \((E_i - O) / n\), the deviation of \(\hat\gamma_i\) from the row-weighted mean of the effects.

Both differences are linear in \(\hat\gamma_i\), so their standard error with \(\hat\beta\) held fixed is \(se(\hat\gamma_i)\) and the limits are those of \(\gamma_i\) shifted.

Examples

d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 20, type = "continuous", seed = 1)
pd <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_linear_fe(pd)
head(standardize(fit, level = 0.95))
#>   provider    observed   expected difference       lower      upper
#> 1     P001  -42.582888 -10.896083 -0.4951063 -0.76938850 -0.2208242
#> 2     P002 -125.896359 -67.439053 -0.2967376 -0.45307196 -0.1404032
#> 3     P003    8.964691  -8.723502  0.3930710  0.06597039  0.7201715
#> 4     P004   34.058194 -43.422138  0.4724410  0.30109834  0.6437838
#> 5     P005   41.090638 -17.888160  0.4834328  0.28477404  0.6820915
#> 6     P006 -101.501224 -39.079480 -0.3001045 -0.45224891 -0.1479602
